1. REGISTRATION

1.1 Sunview Cooperative Housing Society registered under Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960. Record status: current. The Certificate of Registration bearing No. MUM/CHS/1998/4587 was issued by the Deputy Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Thane District, on 14th March 1998.

1.2 The society is a cooperative housing society formed with the object of providing residential accommodation to its members. The society is deemed to be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.

1.3 The society is currently registered and in good standing with the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Maharashtra State. The registration has not been cancelled, suspended, or revoked and continues to be valid as on the date of these bye-laws.

1.4 The society was initially registered with a membership of 42 members and has since grown to its present strength as per the register of members maintained at the registered office.

1.5 The society's financial year shall be from 1st April to 31st March of the following year.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. NAME AND ADDRESS

2.1 The name of the society is SUNVIEW COOPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY (hereinafter referred to as "the Society").

2.2 The registered office of the society is situated at Plot No. 17, Sector 22, Nerul West, Navi Mumbai – 400706, within the jurisdiction of the Thane District Central Co-operative Bank.

2.3 The society may, by a resolution passed at a general meeting and with the prior approval of the Registrar, change its registered office within the city of Navi Mumbai. Any change of address shall be communicated to the Registrar within 30 days of such change.

2.4 All communications, notices, and legal documents shall be served upon the society at its registered office address.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. AREA OF OPERATION

3.1 The area of operation of the society shall be the State of Maharashtra.

3.2 The society shall primarily operate within the limits of Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation, but may undertake activities or hold property anywhere within the State of Maharashtra as permitted under the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960.

3.3 No activity shall be undertaken outside the area of operation without the prior written permission of the Registrar.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. OBJECTIVES

4.1 The main objectives of the society are:

(a) To provide residential accommodation to its members on ownership basis.

(b) To arrange for the maintenance, repair, and upkeep of the building, common areas, and amenities of the society.

(c) To undertake all lawful activities necessary for the welfare and convenience of the members.
(d) A declaration that the applicant shall abide by the bye-laws, rules, and regulations of the society.

5.4 Upon the death of a member, the society shall transfer the membership to the legal heir or nominee upon production of:

(a) A succession certificate from a competent court; or

(b) A probate of the will; or

(c) A legal heirship certificate issued by the appropriate authority; or

(d) An affidavit of succession sworn before a magistrate, accompanied by indemnity bonds as may be required.

5.5 The managing committee shall consider every application for membership within 30 days of receipt. If the application is rejected, the reasons for rejection shall be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant within 15 days of such rejection.

5.6 A member shall cease to be a member of the society in any of the following circumstances:

(a) Upon transfer of his or her interest in the residential unit;

(b) Upon death, subject to the provisions of clause 5.4;

(c) Upon resignation, which shall be accepted only after the member has settled all dues payable to the society; or

(d) Upon expulsion in accordance with the provisions of the Act and these bye-laws.

5.7 The register of members shall be maintained at the registered office of the society and shall contain the name, address, occupation, date of admission, and such other particulars as may be prescribed. The register shall be open for inspection by any member upon request during office hours.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6. RESIDENTIAL UNITS AND ALLOTMENT

6.1 The society's building comprises residential units as described below. According to the society records, Sunview Cooperative Housing Society has total residential units of 120. Record status: current. The distribution of these units is as follows:

(a) Tower A – 40 units, each of 1 BHK configuration, spread over 10 floors with 4 units per floor;

(b) Tower B – 48 units, each of 2 BHK configuration, spread over 12 floors with 4 units per floor;

(c) Tower C – 32 units, each of 3 BHK configuration, spread over 8 floors with 4 units per floor.

6.2 The total number of residential units shall not be increased except by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting at a general meeting, and with the prior approval of the competent authority under the Maharashtra Ownership Flats (Regulation of the Promotion, Construction, Sale, Management and Transfer) Act, 1963.

6.3 Each residential unit shall have a distinct unit number, which shall be noted in the register of units maintained by the society. The unit number shall comprise the tower name, floor number, and unit position on the floor.

6.4 The society shall maintain a register of units containing the following particulars for each unit:

(a) Unit number;

(b) Name of the member to whom the unit is allotted;

(c) Date of allotment;

(d) Area of the unit as per the conveyance deed;

(e) Car parking allotment, if any; and

(f) Remarks, if any.

6.5 No member shall carry out any structural alteration, addition, or modification to his or her residential unit without the prior written permission of the managing committee and, where required, the approval of the municipal authorities. The society may levy a fine for any unauthorised structural work, which shall be recovered as arrears.

6.6 The society may, at a general meeting, decide to undertake redevelopment, repair, or reconstruction of the building. In such an event, the rights and obligations of members shall be governed by the provisions of the Act and the resolutions passed at such meeting.

**PART VII: PROPERTY AND COMMON AREAS**

**7.1** The society shall hold, manage, and maintain the property of the society, which consists of the land, the buildings standing thereon, and all common areas and amenities appurtenant thereto. The property of the society shall be used only for the purposes for which it is intended, and no part thereof shall be alienated, transferred, or otherwise disposed of except in accordance with the provisions of the Act, the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the rules made thereunder, and with the prior approval of the general body by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting.

**7.2** The building plan shows that Sunview Cooperative Housing Society has number of towers of 3. Record status: current. The names of the towers are as follows:

(a) Tower A;
(b) Tower B; and
(c) Tower C.

The number of towers shall not be increased or decreased except by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting at a general meeting, and with the prior approval of the competent authority. The record of the number of towers as stated above is current and shall be updated only upon the completion of any redevelopment or reconstruction as provided in these bye-laws.

**7.3** The common areas and facilities of the society shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

(a) The land on which the buildings are constructed and the land appurtenant thereto;

(b) The staircases, lifts, lobbies, corridors, and entrance halls of each tower;

(c) The compound walls, gates, and boundary of the society;

(d) The internal roads, pathways, and pavements within the society premises;

(e) The parking areas, including open parking and any covered or basement parking, as designated by the managing committee;

(f) The clubhouse, if any, and the amenities therein;

(g) The children's play area and the equipment installed therein;

(h) The garden and landscaped areas, including the lawn, flower beds, and trees;

(i) The water storage tanks, pumps, and the water supply and drainage systems;

(j) The electrical installations, including the main switchboard, distribution panels, and standby generator;

(k) The fire-fighting equipment and the fire alarm system;

(l) The sewage treatment plant, if any, and the associated piping and fittings;

(m) The common lighting, including the lighting of the compound, lobbies, and staircases; and

(n) Any other facility or amenity which is intended for the common use of all members.

**7.5** No member shall, without the prior written permission of the managing committee, do or cause to be done any act which may damage, obstruct, or interfere with the common areas and facilities, or which may cause nuisance or inconvenience to other members. The managing committee may, at its discretion, require any member who causes damage to the common areas or facilities to make good the same, and the cost of such repair shall be recoverable from such member as arrears.

**7.6** The society shall maintain a register of assets in which all movable and immovable assets of the society, including the common areas and facilities described above, shall be recorded. The register of assets shall be kept at the registered office of the society and shall be open for inspection by members during the working hours of the society office.

**7.7** The society shall take out and maintain adequate insurance for the buildings and other insurable assets of the society. The insurance policy shall be kept in the custody of the managing committee, and a copy of the same shall be produced at the annual general meeting for the information of the members.

If the managing committee fails to convene the SGM within the aforesaid period, the requisitionists may themselves convene the meeting in accordance with the Act and Rules.

(c) The notice for an SGM shall be issued in writing at least fourteen clear days before the date of the meeting, specifying the date, time, place, and the special business to be transacted thereat. No business other than that specified in the notice shall be transacted at an SGM, except with the unanimous consent of all the members present.

**8.3 Quorum for General Body Meetings:**

(a) The quorum required for transacting any business at a General Body Meeting, including the Annual General Meeting, shall be as follows:

(i) For the Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Special General Body Meeting (SGM) where ordinary business is transacted, the quorum shall be thirty percent (30%) of the total number of members of the society.

(ii) For the purpose of this bye-law, "total number of members" shall mean the total number of members on the register of members as on the date of the notice of the meeting, excluding those whose membership has been terminated or who are otherwise not entitled to vote.

(b) If within half an hour of the time appointed for the meeting a quorum is not present, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place, or to such other day, time, and place as the chairperson may determine. The notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given to the members by a written notice placed at the society's notice board and/or sent by electronic mode.

(c) At the adjourned meeting, if a quorum is not present within half an hour of the time appointed, the members present shall form the quorum, and they may proceed with the business of the meeting. Provided that for the purpose of passing a special resolution, the quorum shall not be less than one-fifth (20%) of the total number of members, even at an adjourned meeting.

(d) The quorum for the Annual General Meeting 2024 shall be in accordance with sub-clause (a)(i) above, i.e., thirty percent (30%) of the total number of members. For the avoidance of doubt, the quorum required for the AGM 2024 is thirty percent (30%) of the total members, as per the current provisions of these bye-laws. No resolution, other than a procedural motion, shall be moved at any general body meeting unless the requisite quorum is present.
**9. MAINTENANCE, REPAIRS AND IMPROVEMENTS**

**9.1 Obligation to Maintain:**

(a) Every member shall, at their own cost, maintain the interior of their premises, including all internal walls, flooring, sanitary fittings, electrical installations, and fixtures, in good and tenantable condition.

(b) The Society shall be responsible for the maintenance and repair of the common areas, including the main structure of the building, common staircases, lobbies, lifts, water tanks, pumps, drainage lines, sewage lines, compound walls, and the common garden and parking areas.

(c) The Managing Committee may, from time to time, engage contractors, plumbers, electricians, or other professionals for the execution of works connected to the maintenance of the Society's property. The cost of such services shall be met out of the funds of the Society.

**9.2 Periodic Maintenance Fund:**

(a) The Society shall maintain a Sinking Fund, a Repairs and Maintenance Fund, and such other funds as may be required under the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Rules framed thereunder.

(b) Contributions to the Repairs and Maintenance Fund shall be collected from members along with the monthly maintenance charges. The quantum of such contribution shall be determined by the Managing Committee, subject to the approval of the General Body at the Annual General Meeting.

(c) The Managing Committee shall be empowered to sanction expenditure up to an amount of ₹50,000 (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) for urgent repairs without prior approval of the General Body, provided that such expenditure is reported to the General Body at its next meeting.

(d) Any expenditure exceeding ₹50,000 for capital repairs or improvements shall require the sanction of the General Body by an ordinary resolution, unless the work is of an emergency nature, in which case the Managing Committee may undertake the work and seek ratification at the next General Body Meeting.

**9.3 Major Repairs and Renovations:**

(a) For any major repairing or re-construction work, including but not limited to re-roofing, structural repairs, re-plastering of the external facade, replacement of lifts, or overhauling of the water supply and drainage systems, the Managing Committee shall obtain at least three quotations from independent contractors.

(b) The Managing Committee shall present the quotations, along with its recommendations, to the General Body for approval. No work of major repairs shall be commenced without the approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency as provided in bye-law 9.2(d) above.

(c) Upon completion of any major repair work, the Managing Committee shall obtain a completion certificate from the architect or engineer supervising the work, and the accounts pertaining to such work shall be placed before the next Annual General Meeting.

**9.4 Maintenance Charges:**

(a) The monthly maintenance charges shall be levied on all members, including non-resident members, based on the area of the premises occupied by them, as recorded in the Society's register.

(b) The Managing Committee shall have the power to fix, revise, or enhance the monthly maintenance charges, subject to the approval of the General Body. Any revision in the maintenance charges shall be intimated to the members by a written notice at least fifteen (15) days before the due date of payment.

(c) Maintenance charges shall be payable on or before the tenth (10th) day of each calendar month. A member who fails to pay the maintenance charges by the due date shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of eighteen percent (18%) per annum on the amount outstanding, from the date of default until the date of payment.
**10. AMENDMENT OF BYE-LAWS**

**10.1 Power to Amend:**

(a) These Bye-laws may be amended, added to, altered, or rescinded only by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting at a special General Body Meeting convened for the purpose, in accordance with the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Rules, 1961, as amended from time to time.

(b) No amendment shall be effective unless and until it has been duly registered with the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai, as required under the said Act and Rules.

**10.2 Notice of Proposed Amendment:**

(a) Any member desiring to propose an amendment shall give notice in writing to the Honorary Secretary of the Society at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the General Body Meeting at which such amendment is to be considered.

(b) The notice of the proposed amendment shall be circulated by the Managing Committee to all members along with the agenda of the said meeting, not less than fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting.

(c) No amendment shall be considered at a General Body Meeting unless the text of the proposed amendment has been so circulated.

**10.3 Effect of Amendment:**

Upon registration of any amendment with the Deputy Registrar, the amendment shall become effective from the date of such registration, unless the amendment itself specifies a different date of effect, and shall be binding on all members of the Society, including those who may have voted against the amendment or who were absent from the meeting.

**11. DISSOLUTION OF THE SOCIETY**

**11.1 Dissolution by Resolution:**

The Society may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a three-fourths (3/4) majority of the total number of members of the Society, at a special General Body Meeting convened for the purpose, and with the prior approval in writing of the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai.

**11.2 Procedure upon Dissolution:**

Upon the dissolution of the Society, the assets of the Society, after payment of all its debts and liabilities, shall be disposed of in the following manner:

(a) The assets shall be applied first towards the payment of all outstanding dues, taxes, and liabilities of the Society.

(b) The remaining assets, if any, shall be distributed among the members in proportion to the area of the premises owned by each member, as recorded in the Society's register, subject to the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Rules framed thereunder.

(c) No distribution of assets shall be made to any member until all liabilities of the Society have been fully discharged.

**11.3 Appointment of Liquidator:**

Upon the passing of the resolution for dissolution, the General Body shall appoint a Liquidator, who shall be responsible for the winding up of the affairs of the Society, including the collection of all amounts due to the Society, the settlement of all claims against the Society, and the preparation of a final statement of accounts.

**11.4 Final Report:**

The Liquidator shall submit a final report and statement of accounts to the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai, and to the General Body, within a period of six (6) months from the date of his or her appointment, or such extended period as may be permitted by the Deputy Registrar.

**12. INDEMNITY AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY**

**12.1 Indemnity of Committee Members:**

(a) Every member of the Managing Committee, and every officer of the Society, shall be indemnified by the Society against all losses and expenses incurred by him or her in or about the execution of his or her duties, except such losses or expenses as may be occasioned by his or her own wilful act, default, or neglect.

**9. MAINTENANCE, REPAIRS AND IMPROVEMENTS**

**9.1 Obligation to Maintain:**

(a) Every member shall, at their own cost, maintain the interior of their premises, including all internal walls, flooring, sanitary fittings, electrical installations, and fixtures, in good and tenantable condition.

(b) The Society shall be responsible for the maintenance and repair of the common areas, including the main structure of the building, common staircases, lobbies, lifts, water tanks, pumps, drainage lines, sewage lines, compound walls, and the common garden and parking areas.

(c) The Managing Committee may, from time to time, engage contractors, plumbers, electricians, or other professionals for the execution of works connected to the maintenance of the Society's property. The cost of such services shall be met out of the funds of the Society.

**9.2 Periodic Maintenance Fund:**

(a) The Society shall maintain a Sinking Fund, a Repairs and Maintenance Fund, and such other funds as may be required under the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Rules framed thereunder.

(b) Contributions to the Repairs and Maintenance Fund shall be collected from members along with the monthly maintenance charges. The quantum of such contribution shall be determined by the Managing Committee, subject to the approval of the General Body at the Annual General Meeting.

(c) The Managing Committee shall be empowered to sanction expenditure up to an amount of ₹50,000 (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) for urgent repairs without prior approval of the General Body, provided that such expenditure is reported to the General Body at its next meeting.

(d) Any expenditure exceeding ₹50,000 for capital repairs or improvements shall require the sanction of the General Body by an ordinary resolution, unless the work is of an emergency nature, in which case the Managing Committee may undertake the work and seek ratification at the next General Body Meeting.

**9.3 Major Repairs and Renovations:**

(a) For any major repairing or re-construction work, including but not limited to re-roofing, structural repairs, re-plastering of the external facade, replacement of lifts, or overhauling of the water supply and drainage systems, the Managing Committee shall obtain at least three quotations from independent contractors.

(b) The Managing Committee shall present the quotations, along with its recommendations, to the General Body for approval. No work of major repairs shall be commenced without the approval of the General Body, except in cases of emergency as provided in bye-law 9.2(d) above.

(c) Upon completion of any major repair work, the Managing Committee shall obtain a completion certificate from the architect or engineer supervising the work, and the accounts pertaining to such work shall be placed before the next Annual General Meeting.

**9.4 Maintenance Charges:**

(a) The monthly maintenance charges shall be levied on all members, including non-resident members, based on the area of the premises occupied by them, as recorded in the Society's register.

(b) The Managing Committee shall have the power to fix, revise, or enhance the monthly maintenance charges, subject to the approval of the General Body. Any revision in the maintenance charges shall be intimated to the members by a written notice at least fifteen (15) days before the due date of payment.

(c) Maintenance charges shall be payable on or before the tenth (10th) day of each calendar month. A member who fails to pay the maintenance charges by the due date shall be liable to pay simple interest at the rate of eighteen percent (18%) per annum on the amount outstanding, from the date of default until the date of payment.

**10. AMENDMENT OF BYE-LAWS**

**10.1 Power to Amend:**

(a) These Bye-laws may be amended, added to, altered, or rescinded only by a resolution passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members present and voting at a special General Body Meeting convened for the purpose, in accordance with the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Rules, 1961, as amended from time to time.

(b) No amendment shall be effective unless and until it has been duly registered with the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai, as required under the said Act and Rules.

**10.2 Notice of Proposed Amendment:**

(a) Any member desiring to propose an amendment shall give notice in writing to the Honorary Secretary of the Society at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the General Body Meeting at which such amendment is to be considered.

(b) The notice of the proposed amendment shall be circulated by the Managing Committee to all members along with the agenda of the said meeting, not less than fourteen (14) days before the date of the meeting.

(c) No amendment shall be considered at a General Body Meeting unless the text of the proposed amendment has been so circulated.

**10.3 Effect of Amendment:**

Upon registration of any amendment with the Deputy Registrar, the amendment shall become effective from the date of such registration, unless the amendment itself specifies a different date of effect, and shall be binding on all members of the Society, including those who may have voted against the amendment or who were absent from the meeting.

**11. DISSOLUTION OF THE SOCIETY**

**11.1 Dissolution by Resolution:**

The Society may be dissolved by a resolution passed by a three-fourths (3/4) majority of the total number of members of the Society, at a special General Body Meeting convened for the purpose, and with the prior approval in writing of the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai.

**11.2 Procedure upon Dissolution:**

Upon the dissolution of the Society, the assets of the Society, after payment of all its debts and liabilities, shall be disposed of in the following manner:

(a) The assets shall be applied first towards the payment of all outstanding dues, taxes, and liabilities of the Society.

(b) The remaining assets, if any, shall be distributed among the members in proportion to the area of the premises owned by each member, as recorded in the Society's register, subject to the provisions of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, and the Rules framed thereunder.

(c) No distribution of assets shall be made to any member until all liabilities of the Society have been fully discharged.

**11.3 Appointment of Liquidator:**

Upon the passing of the resolution for dissolution, the General Body shall appoint a Liquidator, who shall be responsible for the winding up of the affairs of the Society, including the collection of all amounts due to the Society, the settlement of all claims against the Society, and the preparation of a final statement of accounts.

**11.4 Final Report:**

The Liquidator shall submit a final report and statement of accounts to the Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Mumbai, and to the General Body, within a period of six (6) months from the date of his or her appointment, or such extended period as may be permitted by the Deputy Registrar.

**12. INDEMNITY AND LIMITATION OF LIABILITY**

**12.1 Indemnity of Committee Members:**

(a) Every member of the Managing Committee, and every officer of the Society, shall be indemnified by the Society against all losses and expenses incurred by him or her in or about the execution of his or her duties, except such losses or expenses as may be occasioned by his or her own wilful act, default, or neglect.

NOTES AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR MEMBERS

1. As per the Bye-laws of the Society, the quorum for the Annual General Meeting shall be one-fifth of the total number of members. If the required quorum is not present within half an hour of the scheduled time, the meeting shall be adjourned for half an hour, and the adjourned meeting shall be held at the same venue and on the same day. No quorum shall be required for the adjourned meeting.

4. Only members whose names appear in the register of members of the Society and who have paid their dues up to 31/08/2024 shall be eligible to vote at the meeting. A member who has not paid the maintenance charges for three consecutive months shall not be entitled to vote.

5. Proxy voting is not permitted for the Annual General Meeting as per the Society's Bye-laws.

6. Members are requested to bring this notice and their society identity card to the meeting. Copies of the Annual Report, audited accounts, and budget will be available for inspection at the Society's office from 09/09/2024 to 27/09/2024 between 10:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. and between 5:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. Members may also collect a copy of the Annual Report from the office during the said hours.

The notice announces that Annual General Meeting 2024 is scheduled on 2024-09-28. Record status: current.

7. In case of any change in the date, time, or venue of the meeting due to unforeseen circumstances, members will be informed through a supplementary notice circulated by email and pasted on the notice board.

8. The Managing Committee requests all members to attend the meeting and participate in the discussions to ensure the smooth functioning of the Society.

REPORT OF THE MANAGING COMMITTEE FOR THE FINANCIAL YEAR 2023–24 (SUMMARY)

The Managing Committee is pleased to present a summary of the activities and financial position of the Society for the year ended 31/03/2024.

During the year, the Society collected a total amount of ₹86,42,500 towards maintenance charges from members. The total expenditure for the year amounted to ₹79,18,750, leaving a surplus of ₹7,23,750, which has been transferred to the Repair and Maintenance Fund. The outstanding dues from members as on 31/03/2024 stood at ₹4,86,300, of which an amount of ₹1,12,500 pertains to commercial premises and the remaining ₹3,73,800 pertains to residential premises.

The major repairs carried out during the year included the replacement of the lift rope and controller in Tower A, repair of the water leakage in the basement parking area, and the annual servicing of the fire-fighting system. The society also completed the installation of solar panels on the terrace of Tower B, which has resulted in a reduction of approximately 18% in the common area electricity charges.

The Managing Committee appointed M/s. Kulkarni & Associates, Chartered Accountants, as the internal auditor for the year 2023–24. The internal audit report for the half year ended 30/09/2023 was received on 15/12/2023, and the report for the half year ended 31/03/2024 was received on 20/06/2024. The observations made in the internal audit reports have been noted, and remedial action has been taken in respect of the matters raised therein.

The Society has also been in correspondence with the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation regarding certain notices received in respect of the structure on the terrace of Tower C. The matter has been referred to the Society's advocate, and a detailed response was submitted to the Corporation on 05/08/2024. Members are requested to refer to the notice circulated separately for full details.

MANAGING COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES
SOCIETY NAME: SHIV-SAGAR CO-OPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY LTD.
REG. NO. MUM/SS/2012/456
TOWERS: A, B, C – PLOT 14, SECTOR 22, NERUL, NAVI MUMBAI

MEETING NO. 08/2024 (MONTHLY MEETING)
DATE: 20th August 2024
TIME: 11:00 A.M. TO 1:30 P.M.
VENUE: SOCIETY OFFICE, GROUND FLOOR, TOWER A

MEMBERS PRESENT:
1. Shri. Ramesh Patil – Chairman
2. Smt. Sunita Deshmukh – Vice Chairman
3. Shri. Anil Kulkarni – Secretary
4. Shri. Prakash Joshi – Treasurer
5. Shri. Vijay Nair – Member
6. Smt. Meera Iyer – Member
7. Shri. Suresh Yadav – Member

INVITEES:
1. Shri. Dattatray More – Lift Contractor (Otis Elevator)
2. Shri. Farhan Sheikh – Electrical Contractor

ABSENT WITH APOLOGY:
1. Smt. Kavita Sharma – Member

The meeting was called to order by the Chairman at 11:05 a.m. The minutes of the previous meeting held on 25th July 2024 were read out and confirmed by the members present.

AGENDA ITEM NO. 1: CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES OF THE PREVIOUS MEETING
The minutes of the meeting held on 25th July 2024 were placed before the committee. Smt. Meera Iyer proposed the confirmation of the minutes and Shri. Vijay Nair seconded the same. The minutes were unanimously approved. The Chairman noted that the action items from the previous meeting were under implementation.

AGENDA ITEM NO. 2: UPDATE ON MAINTENANCE CHARGE CIRCULAR
The Secretary informed the committee that the circular regarding the maintenance charge increase and the revised sinking fund contribution was sent to all members by email on 24th July 2024, well before the deadline of 25th July 2024. Physical copies were distributed to senior citizens residing in the society. The circular was also displayed on the notice boards in all three towers. The Secretary reported that a few members expressed concerns regarding the increase and the same was noted. The committee decided that the Chairman will address these concerns during the upcoming general body meeting.

AGENDA ITEM NO. 3: LIFT REPLACEMENT IN TOWER A – FINALISATION
The committee discussed the quotation received from Otis Elevator Company India Ltd. for the replacement of the lift in Tower A. The quotation was as follows:

- Supply and installation of new lift (8-passenger capacity, 13 stops): ₹18,50,000
- Civil works for the lift shaft modifications: ₹2,30,000
- Electrical works: ₹1,20,000
- Total: ₹21,00,000 plus applicable GST

Shri. Dattatray More, the representative from Otis, clarified the technical specifications and the timeline for completion. He informed the committee that the installation would take approximately 10-12 weeks from the date of commencement. The existing lift has been in operation for 22 years and has faced frequent breakdowns, causing inconvenience to the residents, especially senior citizens.

The committee discussed the financial implications. The Treasurer, Shri. Prakash Joshi, informed that the society has sufficient funds in the sinking fund account to cover the expenditure. After detailed discussion, the committee unanimously decided to accept the quotation. The following resolution was passed:

RESOLUTION NO. MC/08/2024/01: RESOLVED that the quotation of M/s. Otis Elevator Company India Ltd. for the supply and installation of a new lift in Tower A at a total cost of ₹21,00,000 plus applicable GST be and is hereby accepted. The Secretary is authorised to sign the agreement and take necessary steps for the commencement of the work.

The committee further decided that the work should commence by 1st September 2024 and requested the Secretary to coordinate with the contractor for the same.

AGENDA ITEM NO. 4: PENDING MAINTENANCE DUES – DEFAULTING MEMBERS
The Treasurer placed before the committee the list of members who have not paid their maintenance charges for the months of May, June, and July 2024. As per the earlier decision, reminder letters were sent to these defaulting members by 18th July 2024. The Treasurer reported that out of the 23 defaulting members, 15 have cleared their dues. The remaining 8 members have not responded.
